skill.name: atxp
skill.description: Use ATXP CLI and MCP services for paid web search, media generation, X search, and PaaS workflows. Authentication is required through ATXP.
skill.summary: Run authenticated ATXP CLI and MCP tools for search, media generation, X search, and PaaS access.
skill.author: atxp-dev

security_audit.summary: The skill is a thin reference for ATXP CLI and MCP services, and most markdown backtick detections are not Ruby execution. Several findings remain valid because the instructions call external npx commands, source a hidden config file, read an ATXP connection token, and contact ATXP network services.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running ATXP commands, and pin or verify the package source when possible.

remediation.issue: Hidden config is sourced from the user home directory.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid sourcing shell files directly; document a safer token-loading method that reads only the required ATXP connection value.

remediation.issue: ATXP connection credentials are read from the environment.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to paste ATXP_CONNECTION into prompts, logs, issues, or generated files.

remediation.issue: Paid and deployment-capable tools may create costs or resources.
remediation.suggestion: Add a confirmation requirement before paid generation, X search, or PaaS deployment actions.

finding_verdicts.reason: The cited description explicitly requires `npx atxp login`, which executes an external npm package during authentication. The markdown backticks are not Ruby execution, but the command instruction is real.
The bash block includes `npx atxp login` and `source ~/.atxp/config`. Running an npm package and sourcing a shell config are real external command actions.
The finding starts at a code-fence close, but its cited range reaches the command table that begins with `npx atxp search <query>`. This is an external CLI command instruction, so it is kept.
Line 25 documents `npx atxp search <query>`, which executes the ATXP CLI and sends a query to an external service. This is intentional but security-relevant command execution.
Line 26 documents `npx atxp image <prompt>`, which runs an external CLI and transmits prompt content for image generation. This is intentional but still an external command risk.
Line 27 documents `npx atxp music <prompt>`, which runs an external CLI and sends user prompt data to a paid service. This is a real external command pathway.
Line 28 documents `npx atxp video <prompt>`, which runs an external CLI and sends prompt content to a video generation service. This is expected but security-relevant.
Line 29 documents `npx atxp x <query>`, which runs the ATXP CLI and sends search terms to an external X search service. This is real external command use.
Line 33 contains markdown-formatted service and skill names, not a shell command or Ruby backtick execution. The PaaS capability is better handled as a semantic business-risk finding.
The cited line uses markdown backticks around an environment variable name. It does not itself execute a command, although nearby sections describe command use separately.
The cited block is TypeScript client sample code, not shell execution. Its network and environment-token behavior are covered by separate static findings.

Line 64 lists an MCP server host and tool name. It does not contain a shell command, Ruby backtick execution, or command substitution.

The TypeScript sample hardcodes `https://search.mcp.atxp.ai` as the MCP server. This is intentional, but it creates outbound network communication to a third-party service.
Line 18 instructs `source ~/.atxp/config`, which reads and executes shell content from a hidden home-directory file. That can load secrets and run arbitrary shell statements.
Line 18 accesses `~/.atxp/config`, a hidden user configuration path likely to contain authentication material. The access is intentional but security-sensitive.
Line 48 reads `process.env.ATXP_CONNECTION` for account authentication. This is expected for the client, but it uses an environment value that may contain a secret token.
Line 48 accesses the environment object to retrieve `ATXP_CONNECTION`. The value appears to be an authentication connection string and should be treated as sensitive.

The exact code reads an environment variable rather than an environment file, but `ATXP_CONNECTION` is used as account credential material. Keeping the sensitive finding is appropriate because the secret is passed into the ATXP client.
Line 3 describes ATXP paid API tools and authentication. It does not request local system discovery, host enumeration, or reconnaissance.
Line 8 states that the skill accesses ATXP paid API tools through a CLI. No local system reconnaissance behavior is described.

content.value_statement: Developers often need search, media generation, and MCP services from one authenticated workflow. This skill documents ATXP CLI and client usage for those paid external tools.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to check ATXP authentication with ATXP_CONNECTION.
Documents login setup using the ATXP CLI.
Lists ATXP commands for web search, images, music, video, and X search.
Provides a TypeScript client example for the ATXP search MCP server.
Lists MCP server hosts and tool names for supported ATXP services.
References ATXP PaaS tools for serverless deployment workflows.
limitations: Requires an ATXP account and valid ATXP_CONNECTION value.
Uses paid external services and may incur charges.
Does not validate command arguments or sanitize prompts.
Delegates detailed PaaS instructions to a separate skill.

use_cases.title: Add Search to Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Use the ATXP search command or MCP server to retrieve current web results for an agent task.

use_cases.title: Create Media from Prompts
use_cases.description: Run authenticated ATXP image, music, or video commands after confirming the prompt and expected cost.

use_cases.title: Explore ATXP PaaS Services
use_cases.description: Review the PaaS endpoint reference before using related tools for functions, databases, storage, and domains.

prompt_templates.title: Check Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the atxp skill to check whether ATXP_CONNECTION is available. If it is missing, explain the login steps without exposing secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Search the Web
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ATXP web search for this query: [query]. Confirm before running the command, then summarize the most relevant results.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Media
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ATXP to create [image, music, or video] from this prompt: [prompt]. Confirm paid tool use before sending the request.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an ATXP client integration for [service]. Include authentication handling, MCP server choice, expected tool call, and security precautions.

output_examples.input: Search for recent information about an API change.
output_examples.output: A concise research summary with source names, dates when available, and a note about uncertain or conflicting results.

output_examples.input: Create an image prompt for a product concept.
output_examples.output: A media request summary that states the selected ATXP tool, final prompt, user confirmation status, and resulting asset location.

output_examples.input: Review whether ATXP PaaS fits a small serverless app.
output_examples.output: A deployment-oriented checklist covering functions, database, storage, domains, analytics, confirmations, and remaining unknowns.

best_practices: Confirm authentication and paid actions before running ATXP commands.
Keep ATXP_CONNECTION out of prompts, logs, issues, and generated files.
Summarize external results with the tool used and any important uncertainty.
anti_patterns: Do not run npx commands in untrusted contexts without confirming the package source.
Do not send secrets, private records, or unnecessary personal data to ATXP tools.
Do not treat search results or generated media as verified without review.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It documents ATXP CLI and MCP usage for paid web search, media generation, X search, and PaaS-related tools.

faq.question: Does it require an ATXP account?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires authentication through ATXP and expects an ATXP_CONNECTION value.

faq.question: Can it run commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes npx ATXP commands, so agents should ask before running them.

faq.question: Does it send data outside my machine?
faq.answer: Yes. Queries and prompts are sent to ATXP services when the related tools are used.

faq.question: Does it include complete PaaS instructions?
faq.answer: No. It references ATXP PaaS capabilities and points to the atxp-paas skill for detailed usage.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
